title: State-machine chip dot is invisible when an option has no colour (bare HSL triple), and the #35911 scan pins only the destructive tokens
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgUkbQqRUUFSiu2HGob

Found by area b1-DB while building #35911 (PR #35961, dev report 7053546276). Same defect family as #35911 item 1, outside that card's scope.

## What the user sees
In the metadata viewer's state-machine panel, each state chip shows a small coloured dot. When the picklist option has no `color`, the dot should fall back to the muted grey. It shows nothing instead: the chip has an empty gap where the dot should be.

## Cause
`ui/packages/components/src/renderers/basic/metadata-viewer.tsx:290` sets `backgroundColor: color ?? 'var(--muted-foreground)'`. The theme stores `--muted-foreground` as a bare HSL triple (`215.4 16.3% 46.9%`), so the value is not a colour and the browser drops the declaration. The fix wraps it: `hsl(var(--muted-foreground))`.

## To do
1. Wrap the fallback in `hsl()` at `metadata-viewer.tsx:290`.
2. Widen the source scan that #35911 adds (`destructive-colour-spelling-35911`) from the destructive tokens to every token the themes store as a bare triple, so any raw `var(--<triple token>)` used as a colour value fails the test. The token list should be read from the theme blocks, not typed by hand, so a new token is covered without editing the test.
3. Fix whatever else the widened scan finds in the same PR, or list it on this card if it is not a colour bug.

## Acceptance
- A state chip whose option has no colour shows the grey dot in light and dark themes.
- The widened scan fails when the wrap is reverted, and passes on the fixed tree.

Blocked-by: #35961 (the scan this card widens lands there).
Reader: area:ux (ui/packages/components).
